hints: Each entry of \(AB\) is a row of \(A\) multiplied by a column of \(B\): multiply matching entries and add.

steps.title: Row by column
steps.explanation: The entry in row \(i\), column \(j\) of \(AB\) comes from row \(i\) of \(A\) and column \(j\) of \(B\).

commonMistakes: Finding \(BA\) instead of \(AB\), which gives option (a); matrix multiplication is not commutative.
Multiplying corresponding entries (as in addition), which gives option (b).
Multiplying rows of \(A\) by rows of \(B\), which gives option (c).

questions.authorNotes: Distractors: (a) = BA, (b) = entry-wise product, (c) = rows of A times rows of B; all computed by script.

content.stem:
Let \[A = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & -3 \\ 1 & 4 \end{bmatrix}, \quad B = \begin{bmatrix} 2 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}, \quad C = \begin{bmatrix} -3 \\ 4 \end{bmatrix}.\] The matrix \(X\) satisfies \(AX = B + 2C\).
(i) Write down the order of the matrix \(X\).
(ii) Find the matrix \(X\).

hints: \(A\) is \(2 \times 2\) and \(B + 2C\) is \(2 \times 1\). What order must \(X\) have for the product \(AX\) to be \(2 \times 1\)?
Let \(X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix}\), multiply out \(AX\) and compare entries to get two simultaneous equations.

solution.modelAnswer: (i) \(X\) is of order \(2 \times 1\). (ii) \(B + 2C = \begin{bmatrix} -4 \\ 9 \end{bmatrix}\). Let \(X = \begin{bmatrix} x \\ y \end{bmatrix}\); then \(2x - 3y = -4\) and \(x + 4y = 9\). Solving, \(y = 2\), \(x = 1\), so \(X = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 2 \end{bmatrix}\).

steps.title: Order of X
steps.explanation: For \(AX\) to exist, \(X\) must have 2 rows (the number of columns of \(A\)); for \(AX\) to be \(2 \times 1\), \(X\) must have 1 column.
steps.rule: An \((m \times n)\) matrix times an \((n \times p)\) matrix is \((m \times p)\).

steps.title: Right-hand side
steps.explanation: Multiply each entry of \(C\) by 2, then add corresponding entries.

steps.title: Multiply and compare
steps.explanation: Equal matrices have equal corresponding entries, so \(2x - 3y = -4\) and \(x + 4y = 9\).

commonMistakes: Taking \(X\) as a \(2 \times 2\) or \(1 \times 2\) matrix; a \(1 \times 2\) matrix cannot be multiplied on the left by \(A\).
Computing \(B + 2C\) as \(\begin{bmatrix} -1 \\ 5 \end{bmatrix}\) by forgetting to double \(C\).
Writing the product as \(\begin{bmatrix} 2x + y \\ -3x + 4y \end{bmatrix}\) (using columns of \(A\) instead of rows).

criteria.description: Forms the product AX and the two equations
criteria.partialCreditRules: Follow-through from an incorrect B + 2C if the product AX is formed correctly.

criteria.expectedEvidence: X = [1, 2] written as a column matrix
acceptedAlternatives: x = 1, y = 2 stated and X written as a column
commonErrors: X written as a row matrix [1 2]

questions.authorNotes: Solved without an inverse matrix (not part of the ICSE Class 10 course as listed in syllabus.json). Answer verified by computing AX.
